## FAQ

### What is the Investing.com Earnings Calendar?

The Earnings Calendar is a free tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide. It displays EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results once released, so you can compare analyst expectations with reported outcomes in a single view.

### What is an earnings surprise? [...] An earnings surprise occurs when a company's reported EPS or Revenue differs from the analyst consensus forecast. A positive surprise means the company outperformed expectations, while a negative surprise means it underperformed. The Earnings Calendar displays this as the EPS Surprise % and Revenue Surprise % columns, making it easy to spot which companies beat or missed forecasts at a glance.

### What does the EPS Revisions column show? [...] Most publicly traded companies report earnings four times a year, once per fiscal quarter. Earnings season typically begins a few weeks after each quarter ends, with the busiest reporting periods falling in January, April, July, and October. Not all companies report on the same date, so the Earnings Calendar helps you track which companies are reporting on any given day.
